name: No Means No Worldwide
beneficiaries_note: Our build: girls taught the No Means No course in 2025 across six countries; NMNW publishes no split, so a judgment from its 2025 report (Nigeria's and Zimbabwe's national scale-ups, South Africa's 90-minute course to tens of thousands, Uganda's partners) and 2024's (Mozambique, Eswatini).
summary: No Means No Worldwide writes a 12-hour school course that teaches girls to recognise, resist and escape sexual assault (and boys to respect consent and step in) and trains local partners and teachers to give it; in 2025 it spent $1.51 million and its partners taught 128,000 young people in six African countries, about half of them a new 90-minute version. Pooled, the three cluster-randomised trials of the girls' course cut rape in the following year by about 31% (risk ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.43-1.11), though the largest, with independent data collectors, found no effect; each rape averted spares about half a healthy year of post-traumatic stress and depression and a small risk of suicide. After adjustments for how the trials were run, delivery at scale and partners' share of the cost, that is about 0.14 years of healthy life per $1,000. The biggest uncertainties are whether the course works at all, how long it protects and how common rape is among the girls taught; the 90-minute course, never tested against a control group, counts at a fifth of the full course's effect and is discounted for missing data.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Young people who took a No Means No course in 2025

source.title: No Means No Worldwide, 2025 Annual Report

rows.explainer: NMNW's own count across six countries (2025 report: Nigeria, Zimbabwe, Uganda and South Africa named, Mozambique from 2024's), delivered by local partners' instructors and teachers NMNW trained. It mixes the standard course (about 12 hours over six weeks) and the new 90-minute 'Worth Defending' version, and girls and boys; the rows below split it. 2024's count was 480,213 before PEPFAR funding to many partners stopped.

rows.label: Share of 2025's young people who took the standard (12-hour) course
rows.explainer: NMNW doesn't split its count. Anchors: 20,685 took the pre/post questionnaire for the full curricula in 2025 (a floor, 16%); the 90-minute course was evaluated with 10,205 participants in uGu District and LifeLine Durban then delivered it to 'tens of thousands' (2025 report); the Zimbabwe, Nigeria and Uganda partners deliver the standard course. Our judgment 55%, 30% to 80%.

rows.label: Girls in the 2025 pre/post questionnaires of the full curricula

source.title: No Means No Worldwide, 2025 Annual Report
source.quote: Through pre/post questionnaires of 14,860 girls and 5,825 boys participating in the full No Means No curricula

rows.explainer: Used only for the share of girls in the standard course.

rows.label: Boys in the 2025 pre/post questionnaires of the full curricula

source.title: No Means No Worldwide, 2025 Annual Report
source.quote: Through pre/post questionnaires of 14,860 girls and 5,825 boys participating in the full No Means No curricula

rows.explainer: Boys take a parallel course on consent, healthy masculinity and stepping in (bystander skills); its effect is inside the trials' effect on girls (below).

rows.label: Share of girls in the standard course
rows.explainer: 72%, from the questionnaire counts.

rows.label: Girls who took the standard course in 2025
rows.explainer: The unit this model counts: girls through the course the trials tested. About 50,000.

rows.label: Share of girls among the 90-minute course's participants
rows.explainer: The 90-minute course was evaluated 'with girls in South Africa' (2025 report) and LifeLine Durban, its main user, works mostly with girls and young women; some partners give it to boys too. Our judgment 85%, 60% to 100%.

rows.label: Girls who took the 90-minute course in 2025
rows.explainer: About 49,000: the rest of the count, girls only.

rows.label: Cost per young person reached, including overhead
rows.explainer: About $12 of NMNW's money per young person; partners' own delivery costs come on top (attribution below).

rows.label: Years the course protects a girl
rows.explainer: The two trials that found an effect measured the 9-10 months after the course; the trial that followed girls for two years found none in the second year (Sarnquist et al. 2024, below). The effect is counted for one year, 0.5 to 2: skills could last longer (most girls who used them said so in Nairobi) or fade within months.

rows.label: Share of girls raped in a year without the course

source.title: Sarnquist et al. (2024), Sexual Assault Among Young Adolescents in Informal Settlements in Nairobi, Kenya: Findings from the IMPower and SOS Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial, Prevention Science 25: 578-589

rows.explainer: The trials' outcome: forced sex in the past 12 months, self-reported. Their control arms at baseline: 6.6% of Nairobi girls aged 10-14 (Sarnquist et al. 2024), 7.3% in Nairobi in 2014 (Baiocchi et al. 2017), 13.8% of Malawi schoolgirls (Decker et al. 2018). 2025's girls are 12 to 18 in Nigeria, Zimbabwe, Uganda and South Africa, many in PEPFAR's programmes for girls at high risk of HIV. Our judgment 8%, 5% to 14%.

rows.label: Risk of rape after the course, against girls without it (pooled risk ratio of the three trials)

source.title: Sarnquist et al. (2024), Sexual Assault Among Young Adolescents in Informal Settlements in Nairobi, Kenya: Findings from the IMPower and SOS Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial, Prevention Science 25: 578-589
source.quote: This study did not show an effect of the intervention on self-reported rape

rows.explainer: Our random-effects pool (DerSimonian-Laird, on log risk ratios) of the three cluster-randomised trials of NMNW's course for girls, each against a standard life-skills class: Nairobi 2014, 3.7 points fewer girls raped from a 7.3% baseline over the 9 months after (95% CI 0.4 to 8.0 points: risk ratio 0.49, log standard error 0.54); Malawi 2016, prevalence 15.2% to 9.2% in the intervention schools (RR 0.59, 0.49-0.72) and 13.8% to 14.5% in controls (RR 1.04, 0.86-1.26), a ratio of 0.57 (log SE 0.14); Nairobi 2016-18, 6.0% against 5.9% raped in the year to 24 months after (odds ratio 1.05, 0.65-1.72, GEE; 1.21, 0.40-5.21, GLMM), the only trial with independent data collectors and linked individual surveys. Heterogeneity is large (Q 5.0 on 2 degrees of freedom, tau-squared 0.10); pooled 0.69, 95% CI 0.43 to 1.11, weights 15%, 49% and 36%. The range runs above 1: the course may do nothing, or a little harm.

rows.label: Deaths a year from rape's consequences, per girl without the course
rows.explainer: Rapes a year times the deaths that follow one (mostly suicide), discounted to when they come.

rows.label: Deaths caused per girl raped (suicide, HIV, pregnancy)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, built up: suicide is the main one. Survivors of sexual assault have markedly higher rates of suicidality (Dworkin et al. 2017); young women's suicide rates in these countries are around 5 to 10 per 100,000 a year, so a doubling for ten years adds about 0.0005 to 0.001. HIV: the attacker is infected and unsuppressed perhaps one time in 50 and forced sex transmits perhaps one time in 100 to 200, and on treatment few die, under 0.00002. Deaths in pregnancy and unsafe abortion add a little. 0.0006, 0.0001 to 0.002.

rows.label: Years from a rape to the middle of its health harms
rows.explainer: Post-traumatic stress is worst in the first months and half of it has gone by a year (Dworkin et al. 2023); depression and suicide risk last longer. Our judgment 1.5 years, 0.5 to 4.

rows.label: Discount for the years until rape's health harms come
rows.explainer: The harms of a rape (post-traumatic stress, depression, later suicide) come over the years after it, discounted at the shared rate from their middle.

rows.label: Share of rapes (and the deaths they cause) the course prevents
rows.explainer: 31% at the pooled trials' best guess, before the adjustments below; below zero in the draws where the course does harm.

rows.label: Other deaths averted per death averted
rows.explainer: 0: every death the course can avert is counted in deaths_per_assault.

rows.label: Deaths averted per girl taught (before adjustments)
Share of deaths averted under age 5
rows.explainer: 0: the girls are 10 to 18.

rows.label: Share aged 5-14 of the deaths averted
rows.explainer: Most of the deaths come years after the rape, when the girls are 15 or older; some girls are 12 to 14. Our judgment 10%, 0 to 30%.

rows.label: Share aged 15-49 of the deaths averted over 15
rows.explainer: All: the deaths counted come within about ten years of a rape in adolescence.

rows.label: Rapes averted per girl taught (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Girls not raped in the year after the course, per girl taught: 8% times 31%, about 0.025.

rows.label: Years of post-traumatic stress disorder per girl raped, beyond what she'd have anyway

source.title: Dworkin, Jaffe, Bedard-Gilligan and Fitzpatrick (2023), PTSD in the Year Following Sexual Assault: A Meta-Analysis of Prospective Studies, Trauma, Violence, & Abuse 24(2): 497-514
source.quote: Estimated PTSD prevalence was 74.58% at the first month and 41.49% at the twelfth month following sexual assault

rows.explainer: The meta-analysis of 22 prospective samples: 75% meet PTSD criteria a month after a sexual assault and 41% after a year, so about 0.55 of the first year; those still ill at a year mostly have chronic PTSD lasting years more (we judge 3, 1.5 to 6, for the 41%), less the 5-10% a year who would have it anyway. 1.6 years, 0.8 to 3. The studies are mostly of adult women in the US; adolescents in poor settings get less care (wider range).

rows.label: Share of that PTSD at GBD's severe level
rows.explainer: GBD values PTSD as an anxiety disorder; the rest at its moderate level. Symptom severity averaged 48% of the scales' maximum a month after and 30% after a year (Dworkin et al. 2023). Our judgment 20%, 5% to 40%.

rows.label: Disability weight of the PTSD
rows.explainer: GBD 2019's weights for moderate (0.133) and severe (0.523) anxiety disorder, mixed by the share above: about 0.21.

rows.label: Extra years of depression per girl raped, beyond the PTSD

source.title: Dworkin, Menon, Bystrynski and Allen (2017), Sexual assault victimization and psychopathology: A review and meta-analysis, Clinical Psychology Review 56: 65-81
source.quote: Sexual assault was associated with increased risk for all forms of psychopathology assessed

rows.explainer: Survivors are more often depressed than others (the meta-analysis: worse psychopathology of every kind, Hedges' g about 0.6), much of it alongside the PTSD already counted. Our judgment of the depression beyond it: 0.4 years at a moderate episode, 0.1 to 1.2.

rows.label: Healthy years lost per girl raped (illness only)
rows.explainer: Post-traumatic stress and depression, discounted to when they come: about 0.47. Deaths are counted separately, by age; injuries, pregnancies, infections and schooling lost are in the unmodelled share.

rows.label: Illness averted as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer: 0: illness is counted once, in DALYs (dalys_illness_averted_per_person).

rows.label: Stillbirths averted per girl taught
rows.explainer: 0: pregnancies from rape are in the unmodelled share.

rows.label: Later-life income gain per girl taught, ln(consumption) per year
rows.explainer: 0: no study measures income; schooling kept by avoiding pregnancy is in the unmodelled share.

rows.label: Years until the income gain starts
rows.explainer: Unused (no income gain is modelled); the template's shared figure is kept so the row means the same in every model.

rows.label: Years the long-term income gain lasts
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for how long a long-term income gain lasts (GiveWell's working years, 40), read by every model that counts one (INV-13).

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, present value
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate, the wait included, so the result moves with it. Never type in a present value worked out elsewhere: rebuild it from its inputs.

rows.label: Resource sharing within households (multiplier on an earner's gain)
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (GiveWell's): an earner's income gain is shared with the household, so it counts this many times. Read by every model that values a long-term income gain (INV-13).

rows.label: Internal validity of the pooled trial effect
rows.explainer: In the two trials that found an effect (64% of the pool's weight), the course's own instructors gave out the surveys and the surveys weren't linked person to person, which their authors say may have changed how girls reported; the trial with independent collectors found no effect, and its authors note that girls with the most rapes at baseline dropped out more. The pool already counts the null trial, so this is the bias left in the other two. Our judgment 0.7, 0.4 to 1.

rows.label: External validity: 2025's partners and countries against the trials'
rows.explainer: The trials ran in Nairobi and Malawi in 2014-2018 with Ujamaa-Africa's experienced instructors; 2025's courses are in Nigeria, Zimbabwe, Uganda and South Africa, by HIV-programme partners, community instructors and classroom teachers NMNW certified, for girls 12 to 18, much like the trials' ages. Our judgment 0.8, 0.5 to 1.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: The product of its two parts.

rows.label: Share of the effect that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: The trials' effect is already net of a standard life-skills class. Some girls would otherwise have had another violence-prevention or HIV-programme curriculum (PEPFAR's DREAMS partners run several). Our judgment 80%, 60% to 100%.

rows.label: Partners' and governments' own delivery cost per young person taught
rows.explainer: Instructors and teachers paid by partners' other funders (PEPFAR, UN Women, governments) teach classes of 15 to 30 for 12 hours, plus preparation, supervision and travel: a few hours of local staff time per girl at a few dollars an hour; the 90-minute course far less. NMNW's own $266,421 of grants to partners is already in its cost. Our judgment $4 a young person, $1.50 to $10.

rows.label: NMNW's share of the resources behind the courses
rows.explainer: NMNW's spending over its own plus partners' and governments' delivery costs (Convention 2): about 75%.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (fidelity and completion)
rows.explainer: The trials' effects are by school, every enrolled girl counted; at scale some girls counted miss sessions, and partner delivery may be less faithful than in the trials (NMNW certifies and monitors instructors, and requires partners' quarterly reports). Our judgment 85%, 60% to 100%.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: NMNW's money draws in partners' and governments' delivery (Zimbabwe's education ministry adopted the course, Nigeria's National Youth Service Corps is to deliver it) and trainers it certifies keep teaching; against that, a funder that would have paid for the course anyway. Our judgment 1, 0.85 to 1.2.

rows.label: Years a donation waits before NMNW spends it
rows.explainer: Unrestricted net assets of $685,864 at the end of 2025 (statement of financial position, p. 3) against $1.51 million of spending: about 5 months. 0.5, 0.25 to 1.

rows.label: Years from NMNW's spending to the course reaching girls
rows.explainer: Instructor training and partner grants come months before the classes. 0.5, 0.25 to 1.

rows.label: Years from delivery to the middle of the protection
rows.explainer: The benefits come over the years of protection (a net's life, a season's doses), so they are discounted from its middle; 0 for a one-off effect such as a vaccine dose's.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the benefits come
rows.explainer: Every wait is discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit (the income gain's own wait is counted from delivery, in ln_income_gain_per_person).

rows.label: Standard course: counted less where the outcome isn't measured
rows.explainer: Measured: NMNW counts the young people it reaches, and its own course for girls was tested in three cluster-randomised trials against a standard class, delivered the same way (trained local instructors in schools).

rows.label: 90-minute course: counted less where the outcome isn't measured
rows.explainer: Thin: the 90-minute course has only pre/post questionnaires, no controlled measure of rape, so its effect is a judgment and the shared missing-data step applies.

rows.label: All adjustments, standard course
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * full_missing_data_adj

rows.label: All adjustments, 90-minute course
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * short_missing_data_adj

rows.label: Standard course's share of the unadjusted outcome
rows.explainer: The standard course's share of the illness averted, for the averages below only.

rows.label: Missing-data step: outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the two branches' markers, for reading only; each branch applies its own.

rows.label: All adjustments: outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches' total adjustments, for reading only: the outcome rows apply each branch's own.

rows.label: Treatment costs averted, as a share of value
rows.explainer: 0: few survivors here reach post-rape care (most disclose to friends or family, Baiocchi et al. 2017), and its cost is small against the healthy years; GiveWell's prevention share is for malaria.

rows.label: Rebound effects, as a share of value lost
rows.explainer: 0: no immunity is lost; the malaria rebound doesn't apply.

rows.label: Investment of income increases, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: 0: no income gain is modelled.

rows.label: Other effects: pregnancy, infection, injury, schooling, boys' own safety, disclosure
rows.explainer: Each rape averted also averts some pregnancies (and unsafe abortions), sexually transmitted infections and injuries, and schooling lost; boys in the course (about 28% of the standard course) may be abused less themselves (1 in 7 before 18, 2025 report); and girls already abused disclose more and are linked to care (Malawi's trial referred 172 to a survivors' group). Against these, a girl blamed or retaliated against for resisting, or a false sense of safety. Our judgment +15% of the modelled value, -5% to +40%; a side effect, weighed by the shared slider.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: GiveWell-style supplementary adjustments, each its own row, summed: they add to the modelled value as one share, as in GiveWell's sheets.

rows.label: Deaths averted, standard course
Deaths averted, 90-minute course
Rapes averted
rows.explainer: Girls spared a rape in the year after the course, both courses, after every adjustment. For reading.

rows.label: Deaths averted
Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's moral weights for the age band of each death averted (under five, 5–14, 15–49, 50 and over), times your multiplier on the value of a life: the site's one value of a death (docs/normalization.md 2.7).

rows.label: Units of value from deaths averted
Units of value from stillbirths averted
rows.explainer: 0: no stillbirth channel is modelled (stillbirths_averted_per_person is 0).

rows.label: Units of value from later-life income
rows.explainer: 0: no income gain is modelled (ln_income_gain_per_year is 0).

rows.label: Units of value from illness averted
rows.explainer: A share of the deaths' and income's value, the base GiveWell's supplementary share has.

rows.label: Illness averted per girl taught, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Rapes averted times the illness one causes.

rows.label: The 90-minute course's effect on rape, against the standard course's
rows.explainer: 'Worth Defending' keeps the mental and verbal skills of the 12-hour course and drops the physical ones; it was evaluated only by pre/post questionnaires (10,205 girls in uGu District: knowledge 26% to 84%), not against a control group or on rape. The trials' control girls had a 1.5-2 hour life-skills class, about this dose, and the effect is net of it. Our judgment 20% of the standard course's effect, 5% to 50%.

rows.label: Illness averted, standard course, in DALYs
Illness averted, 90-minute course, in DALYs
Illness averted, in DALYs
Illness averted, in units of value
rows.explainer: The bridge from DALYs into units of value: the unit's conversion cancels it, so illness counts as healthy years whatever "Healthy year vs doubled-income year" is set to.

rows.label: Total units of value
rows.explainer: Illness and the other supplementary shares add to the modelled value side by side, as one sum of shares does in GiveWell's sheets; illness counted in DALYs comes in through its bridge, inside the side-effect share like every other outcome.
